A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PointVid augmentation and regularization framework. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-generation evaluations, qualitative component ablations, synthetic point-cloud examples, and a 10-labeler user study, including results in its appendices.

after.justification: v2 reports original evaluations of UNet and DiT implementations, numerical point-reconstruction and component-ablation results, additional benchmark results, and the retained user-study outcomes.

M1.justification: v1 implements the framework with a UNet, whereas v2 adds a CogVideoX 1.5 DiT implementation, substantially extending the implemented model architectures. Appendix A.2 also specifies regularization every five iterations, qualifying v1's per-step description. The point-processing pipeline and core loss components remain unchanged; the explicit two-pass cross-attention description is additional implementation detail.

E1.justification: Appendix A.4 adds evaluation using the official VBench test batch; v1 used VBench metrics on a Panda70M test batch. Otherwise, the Panda70M/internal training sources, Kubric examples, and task-oriented/general-video domains remain. Increased sample counts and additional backbone configurations do not themselves expand task coverage.

E2.justification: v1's quantitative Table 1 compares only against I2VGen-XL. v2 adds SVD, LTX Video, and CogVideoX 1.5 to that comparison and evaluates the proposed DiT model against its corresponding backbone. Figure 1 also adds CogVideoX 1.5 and LTX Video; DynamiCrafter remains a qualitative comparator.

E3.justification: The reported training collection increases from approximately 70K to 100K videos. The main test batch changes from 387 clips to 372 images, with random initial-frame selection now specified; the user study is also tied to this revised batch. v2 adds a 1360×768, 48-frame DiT configuration alongside the retained 448×256, 16-frame UNet configuration, plus point-MSE evaluation, quantitative ablations, and an official VBench-batch evaluation.

E4.justification: v1 already tests point augmentation, regularization, cross-attention, and diffusion loss qualitatively, including Appendix C. v2 adds numerical subject/background-consistency measurements for these ablations in Table 3 and directly evaluates point-trajectory reconstruction before training, without regularization, and with regularization in Table 2. These substantially strengthen component and mechanism analysis beyond relocating existing illustrations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, generation seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. Both retain 10 human labelers and report aggregate preference fractions without uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces the I2VGen-XL/UNet physical-commonsense scores of 0.32665/0.37434 with 0.32876/0.37805 under revised settings, so this is not a same-setting performance gain. New results include DiT physical commonsense of 0.41384 versus CogVideoX's 0.36549, point MSEs of 0.2125/0.0031/0.0020, quantitative ablations, and official-batch scores. Qualitative examples are also added or replaced. The user-study percentages remain identical between v1 Table 2 and v2 Table 5.

T1.justification: The reconstruction, rigidity, and combined-loss equations retain their mathematical content. Renaming the diffusion-loss term from Lddim to Ldiff does not introduce a new derivation. Neither version provides formal theorems or proofs, and the added standard MSE evaluation does not introduce new theory.

C1.justification: The three principal contributions—point augmentation, 3D regularization, and PointVid—are retained. v2 drops the introduction's explicit claim of accurately resolving dynamic contacts and emphasizes visual plausibility and integration across video models. This modestly recalibrates the claimed outcome rather than replacing the central contribution.

C2.justification: Section 5 adds an explicit motion-magnitude versus smoothness trade-off. Appendix A.2 explains that excessive regularization suppresses motion, whereas excessive diffusion-loss dominance permits artifacts, and discusses balancing these effects. The limitations also shift from future transformer adoption to larger backbones and improved tracking. These are substantive but focused qualifications of the retained interpretation.

D1.justification: New Appendix A.2 documents the equal Panda70M/internal-data mixture, 640×360 two-second source clips, backbone-specific configurations, A100 80GB hardware, loss scheduling, and computational overhead: approximately 9 versus 4.75 seconds per iteration and less than 2GB additional memory. Section 3.2 clarifies bidirectional cross-attention and inference inputs. Conversely, v2 omits v1's project-page link and explicit ZoeDepth dependency disclosure.

R1.justification: v2 adds a focused concurrent-work discussion distinguishing its 3D representation from VideoJam's optical flow and Track4Gen's 2D correspondence. It also adds references to LTX Video, DDIM, DELTA, and SpatialTrackerV2, while removing ZoeDepth. Most related-work discussion and the overall research positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and substantial portions of the introduction and method are retained. v2 revises the abstract and experimental narrative, clarifies training versus inference, incorporates former appendix ablation discussion into Section 4.3, and reorganizes the supplement into A.1–A.5. These are localized narrative and organizational revisions rather than a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column presentation with an opening comparison page to a single-column conference layout. Comparison figures are substantially rearranged, the dataset workflow becomes horizontal, and a dual-backbone comparison is introduced. Existing ablation panels are redistributed across Figures 6–7. Table 1 expands, three new numerical tables appear, and the existing user-study table moves to Table 5.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's narrow quantitative comparison and reliance on qualitative component evidence through additional comparators, a second architecture, point-reconstruction measurements, and numerical ablations. Implementation and computational disclosures, together with the motion-suppression discussion, improve reproducibility and interpretation. Reporting ambiguities remain: full-UNet scores differ between Tables 1 and 3, and user-study percentages are unchanged despite the revised test batch. These limitations temper, but do not outweigh, the substantial gains in empirical support and transparency.
